claim: arch_changeset_builder.md:87, the Cleanup op shape table: `deps | none — the finished task the cleanup follows is not named; the journal's removed event is the tie`, on the premise of arch_action_classifier.md:12 that an absent task means `the repository now holds code answering to no spec node`. More generally, the batch order the plan module states is sort order only: arch_topological_sorter.md:9 fixes three type tiers (`proposal epic first, then features + data_flow tasks, then multi-component test tasks`), plan/sorter.go:13 holds them as a private map `tierOf` whose comment (:12) says a NodeType absent from it `belongs to no tier`, and the builder derives every create's deps from the spec graph alone (arch_action_classifier.md:13, DepSpecNodeIDs). No tier boundary becomes a `blocks` edge, so the order never reaches the tracker, `br ready` does not know it, and the profile that declares node kinds (schema/defaultProfile.json) has no way to place a kind it adds.
authoritative_source: spec/proposals/2026-08-31-task-lifecycle.md:39 defines component renames as delete+create (`BeadReader` -> `TaskReader`); :59 prices that as `an old-node close and a new create in the mint`. In a rename the deleted half's code is still called by a live node until the created half and the caller's own change land. arch_action_classifier.md:95 calls the data_flow add-on `the contract layer` — the flow is the contract the components it names implement against — yet only the components a flow names wait for it. The undecided cases: what a cleanup depends on when the code it deletes is still called; what any task depends on when the kind order is meant to hold in the tracker, not only in the changeset file; and where a profile-declared kind sits in that order.
evidence: Bead spexmachina-swvx.7 (`Code cleanup: plan/BeadReader`), PR #467. `cmd/spex/plan.go:107` still calls `plan.ReadBeadsBytes`; the created half `spexmachina-swvx.14` (TaskReader) and the caller's bead `spexmachina-swvx.21` (PlanCommand, owner of `--beads`) are both open. Because the cleanup op was minted with `deps: none`, `br ready` listed swvx.7 before either, and deleting `plan/bead_reader.go` breaks `go build ./...`. The bead has no legal outcome under the current leaves: not implementable (the deletion needs swvx.21's code, out of scope), not a spec defect the implementer could name in its own contract, not approvable (a PR carrying only a `blocks` edge would close the only bead tracking the deletion). Five review rounds in faber run 20260903-114514 restated that and the loop exhausted; the edge `swvx.7 blocks-on swvx.21` had to be added by hand.
proposed_fix: Make the kind order profile data, and make the builder turn it into edges. (1) Profile: an ordered list of the plan-relevant kinds (default: data_flow, component, test_section). The proposal epic is first and the cleanup pseudo-kind last by rule, outside the list. The profile schema requires every plan-relevant kind exactly once; the builder refuses a batch that carries a kind the list does not place, instead of the sorter's silent `belongs to no tier`. (2) arch_changeset_builder.md, deps: every create op depends on every create op of the previous non-empty layer, as `ref:op`, in addition to its spec-graph deps; the cleanup layer also names each retarget op's target as `ref:task`. Adjacent layers only — the tracker's blocking is transitive, so a test blocked on every feature is blocked on every flow. A layer is a barrier by being in the list; there is no per-entry flag. Cycle-free by construction: edges point only at earlier layers. (3) arch_topological_sorter.md: file order is the declared order, epic first and cleanups last, so every `ref:op` is in the adapter's substitution table before its dependent. `op_id` is derived from a canonical key (layer, spec_node_id), not from file position, so reordering the profile does not change the journal event ids ingest derives from `(git_head, op_id)`. (4) arch_action_classifier.md:12: `code answering to no spec node` -> `code answering to no spec node, or to the removed half of a rename whose successor and callers have not yet landed`; the data_flow add-on at :95 stays as the precise relation beside the layer edges. Cost, accepted: a task waits for the whole previous layer, not only the nodes it relates to; the layer edges are the same trade the cleanup rule makes — a rule that can only over-wait over one that can under-wait silently.
